analyzed_vuln.description: After `htmlParseContentInternal(ctxt)` returns, `htmlParseDocument` unconditionally expands `CUR` at line 4886 and dereferences `ctxt->input->cur`, even when content parsing has stopped the parser or otherwise returned after input-buffer growth/error handling. During the final `GROW` in `htmlParseContentInternal` (line 4772), `xmlParserGrow` can reach `xmlParserInputBufferGrow` and `xmlBufGrowInternal`, whose successful `realloc` moves and frees the old input buffer. In this PoV the post-parse cursor used by the unconditional `CUR` remains associated with that freed allocation, producing the one-byte UAF. The patch-relevant defect is the missing parser-state/input-validity guard around the post-content `CUR` access in `htmlParseDocument`; it must not inspect the cursor after parsing has stopped or returned with an invalid input state.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The HTML pull-parser harness consumes the first four bytes as parser options and the next four as the fuzz allocation limit, then passes all remaining bytes to `htmlCtxtReadMemory`. A sufficiently long, malformed HTML body must make `htmlParseContentInternal` consume enough callback-backed input that its trailing `GROW` requests more data with fewer than `INPUT_CHUNK` bytes remaining. The growth must successfully reallocate and move the decoded input buffer, while the selected allocation limit and malformed parsing state cause content parsing to stop/return before `htmlParseDocument` performs its autoclose check. `htmlParseDocument` then evaluates `CUR == 0` despite the stopped/invalid state and reads one byte through the stale cursor.

patch_result.patch:
--- a/HTMLparser.c
+++ b/HTMLparser.c
@@ -4883,7 +4883,7 @@
     /*
      * autoclose
      */
-    if (CUR == 0)
+    if ((PARSER_STOPPED(ctxt) == 0) && (CUR == 0))
 	htmlAutoCloseOnEnd(ctxt);

args: In libxml2/HTMLparser.c, what exact parser-state and input-validity guard should htmlParseDocument use immediately after htmlParseContentInternal(ctxt) before evaluating CUR and calling htmlAutoCloseOnEnd? Please compare analogous code and explain PARSER_STOPPED semantics and whether checking ctxt->input or cur/end is necessary.

The reported ASan UAF occurs at libxml2/HTMLparser.c:4886, where htmlParseDocument unconditionally evaluates CUR after htmlParseContentInternal. The final GROW in htmlParseContentInternal at line 4772 can realloc the input buffer and parsing can stop or return with stale cursor state. The vulnerability description explicitly says the missing parser-state/input-validity guard around the post-content CUR access is patch-relevant. I am considering `(PARSER_STOPPED(ctxt) == 0) && (ctxt->input != NULL) && (CUR == 0)`, but need determine established project conventions and whether stopped state alone guarantees avoiding invalid input.
